issues.legal_issue: A provision declaring that a Hindu marriage is not invalid solely because the spouses belong to different castes applies to marriages celebrated before the provision was enacted.
material_facts: The courts found that a Hindu marriage had taken place between a woman found by the trial court to be Brahmin and a man who was Shudra.
The marriage took place before the Hindu Marriages Validity Act, 1949 came into force.
The validity of the marriage was challenged on the ground that the spouses belonged to different castes.
issues.conclusion: The marriage was retrospectively validated by section 3 of the Hindu Marriages Validity Act, 1949, even if the spouses belonged to different castes.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Hindu Marriages Validity Act, 1949, provides that no Hindu marriage is invalid, or is to be deemed ever to have been invalid, solely because the parties belonged to different religions, castes, sub-castes or sects. The Court held that this language operates retrospectively. No earlier judicial cases were relied on. Section 1 of the Hindu Widows' Re-Marriage Act, 1856, was discussed by way of comparison; the Court treated its express reference to the legitimacy of the issue as abundant caution, not as a requirement for validating a marriage to have that consequence.

predicates.hindu_marriage_validity_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a Hindu marriage is valid.
predicates.spouses_belong_to_different_castes: The spouses belonged to different castes.
predicates.marriage_predated_validating_law: The marriage took place before a later law declared that marriages were not invalid solely because spouses belonged to different castes.
predicates.intercaste_marriage_is_valid: The marriage is valid despite the spouses belonging to different castes.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns the validity of a Hindu marriage between spouses of different castes and the marriage predates a law validating such marriages, the marriage is treated as valid.

issues.legal_issue: Retrospective validation of an inter-caste Hindu marriage makes a child born of that marriage legitimate and entitled to coparcenary rights.
material_facts: A child was born of the marriage before the Hindu Marriages Validity Act, 1949 came into force.
The child sued for partition, claiming membership in the joint Hindu family and a share in its property.
The courts found that the marriage and the child's birth from it had been proved.
issues.conclusion: The child was legitimate and had the rights of a coparcener in relation to the joint family property.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3 of the Hindu Marriages Validity Act, 1949, a marriage between Hindus is not invalid solely because the parties belonged to different castes, and the provision retrospectively validated marriages celebrated before its enactment. The Court held that legitimacy necessarily follows from the marriage's validity; the legislature's purpose included legitimizing children of those marriages. The express reference to the issue's legitimacy in section 1 of the Hindu Widows' Re-Marriage Act, 1856, was only abundant caution. No earlier judicial cases were relied on.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The proceeding is a claim for partition of joint family property.
predicates.child_born_of_intercaste_hindu_marriage: A child was born of a Hindu marriage between spouses belonging to different castes.
predicates.marriage_predated_validating_law: The marriage took place before a later law declared that marriages were not invalid solely because spouses belonged to different castes.
predicates.child_is_legitimate_coparcener: The child is legitimate and has coparcenary rights in the joint family property.

issues.definition: If a partition proceeding concerns a child born of an inter-caste Hindu marriage that predates a law validating such marriages, the child is treated as legitimate and entitled to coparcenary rights.
